scope: All returned speech plus relevant actual tool results; no desktop frontend or external-business execution was tested.

findings.detail: A personal arrangement triggered save/check calls for draft_v1 and draft_v2. The first immutable draft was populated with a personal memo and dummy cost fields, and both checks failed. At step 2 the correct project v1 write conflicted with that existing draft; saving the v1 values as draft_v2 then failed the v2 checker. The assistant disclosed the conflict and check failure, but did not fulfill the requested draft_v1 artifact. This failure remains in the 24-artifact denominator.

The retrieved episode summary says the user asked whether to revise and recheck, whereas the original step-2 speech shows that follow-up question was asked by the assistant. This attribution was not the target of a scored probe, so it is reported separately. The latest-arrangement answer still follows the correct original timeline.

The acknowledgement repeats the user personal arrangement as remind me to carry the orange card, without marking it as a quotation. The later scored probe 14 correctly attributes the latest arrangement to the user; this earlier phrasing issue is retained separately.

These distractor turns requested one short suggestion. The model added a second paragraph acknowledging scenario boundaries. The statements did not claim real execution or change task facts; the extra prose is retained as an unscored instruction-following issue.
The final plan itself is correct and checked, but the accepted plaintext answer begins with unsolicited English discussion of evidence sufficiency and host formatting instructions.

The personal-arrangement turn again saved a dummy personal memo into immutable draft_v1. On the project turn, the correct v1 write conflicted; saving v1 values into draft_v2 then failed that checker. A later chat request hit the provider-usage guard, so the turn has no returned speech. The earlier wrong writes remain task-quality failures independent of the usage interruption.
